prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A request with no key or an unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`; a known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`. The three roles are viewer (reads only), cook (also cook, waste, temperatures and stock-take counts) and manager (everything). Every non-GET request with a known key writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status), including ones that fail, such as a 403 or a 409. Managers read the log newest first at `GET /audit`. `data/seed.json` has three development keys, one per role: `dev-viewer-key`, `dev-cook-key` and `dev-manager-key`. The test helper now sends the manager key by default, and the new `tests/auth.test.js` covers 401, 403, each role's permissions and the audit log. `npm test` (31 passing) and `npm run lint` both pass. Five things to know: (1) I left `data/db.json` alone, so until you add `apiKeys` to it, `npm start` will answer 401 to every request. (2) I did not bump the schema version; `apiKeys` and `audit` are optional collections, like `outbox`. (3) A data-changing request now writes the file twice: once in the route, then once more for its audit entry. (4) Requests that fail authentication (401) are not audited, because there is no key name to record. (5) Keys are stored in plain text in the data file, as the task described.
